dwelling_habits.dwelling: Open ocean and coastal bays; powerful jaws for hard prey.
dwelling_habits.food: Crabs, conchs, and other crunchy invertebrates.
dwelling_habits.feeding: Big head and jaws crack shells other turtles can’t.
dwelling_habits.mating: Famous nesting beaches; females may travel huge distances.
dwelling_habits.socializing: Solitary travelers between feeding and nesting grounds.

fun_facts: The logger head is packed with muscle for shell-cracking.
Hatchlings use Earth’s magnetic field like a built-in GPS.

dwelling_habits.dwelling: Reef crevices and rocky bottoms; spines wave in the surge.
dwelling_habits.food: Algae — a key grazer that helps coral stay clear.
dwelling_habits.feeding: Night grazing marches across reef rock.
dwelling_habits.mating: Broadcast spawners; larvae drift before settling.
dwelling_habits.socializing: A 1980s die-off changed Caribbean reefs — recovery still matters.

fun_facts: Step carefully: spines are brittle and painful.
When Diadema vanish, algae can smother coral.
